name: Rhi Magnesita India Ltd
title: Rhi Magnesita India Ltd - 534076 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 9% to INR 4,000+ crores, a record, but Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 12.1% and goodwill on Dalmia assets was impaired.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue from operations grew 9% YoY to INR 4,000 crores on 5% higher shipments of 523 kilotons, the company's highest ever. Q4 revenue was INR 932 crores, hit by geopolitical disruption and a soft cement cycle, with adjusted EBITDA of INR 113 crores (12.1% margin) and adjusted PAT of INR 39 crores before exceptionals. Full-year adjusted EBITDA was INR 477 crores at 11.9% margin versus 13.7% in FY25, and a goodwill impairment on the RHIM IR (Dalmia) assets was booked in the quarter. Management guided to about 13% EBITDA margin for FY27, with price increases of 1-3% from May and a strong coke oven order book.

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted PAT before exceptional items (Q4 FY26)

segments.name: Dalmia assets (RHIM IR)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 1,153 crores vs INR 1,013 crores in FY25 (+14%); EBITDA margin 10.8% vs 11.5%. Goodwill impairment booked in Q4 on these assets only.

segments.name: Cement
segments.commentary: Cement fell to about 11% of revenue in FY26 from about 13% in FY25 as management chose not to chase low-margin business amid competitor overcapacity (Calderys, IFGL).

segments.name: Iron making / coke oven and DRI
segments.commentary: Secured a 30,000+ tonne order for 2 coke oven batteries with a large integrated steel customer, covering about 15-18 months; mines now transferred into company name, which management says lowers input cost versus buying at roughly double mining cost.

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: Largest segment; growth driven by ladle solutions, EAF projects, tundish and ladle slide gate solutions. India-wide steel capacity cited at about 165 million tonnes.

guidance_outlook: FY27 full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guided at about 13%, with Q1 FY27 expected to be stronger than the FY26 average.
Volume growth to outperform the market by 1-2 percentage points (management cited 6-7% market growth, implying about 9% company volume growth).
Price increases of 1-3% sought from May 2026 onwards, depending on segment, to offset input cost inflation; some double-digit increases reportedly secured in certain products.
FY27 capex of about INR 150 crores, of which maintenance capex is INR 40-50 crores; to be funded from balance sheet, with no large transactions planned.
Management stated no further restructuring is required.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR 135 crores, focused on operational excellence, innovation, selective capacity, automation and sustainability.
FY26 spend on Dalmia asset modernisation about INR 100 crores; FY27 capex about INR 150 crores, which also includes Bhiwadi and Jamshedpur.
Two robotic systems operating in caster operations (India's first fully integrated caster robotics solution); further automation expected in coming years.
Coke oven batteries: 5 more expected in next 2-3 years, management expects to win at least 2 of them.
demand_pricing: Management says the refractory industry faces excess capacity, aggressive pricing, and rising raw material, freight and energy costs.
Magnesia-based products (fused magnesia, DBM) saw high-cost inventory and energy and freight increases from China, which hit Feb and March shipments.
Management says Q4 volumes were soft due to the seasonal cement lean period (October to January); Q3 was in line.
Management says the company's volume growth (about 5%) in FY26 was slightly below a market growth of about 6%.
Export volumes declined significantly; imports and new competitor capacity added pressure, in management's view.

qa_highlights.question: Is the restructuring complete, what was the goodwill impairment, and what is the FY27-FY28 roadmap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said restructuring is complete and only the Dalmia assets were impaired, citing lower export volumes, INR/USD volatility on USD-denominated raw materials, and new competitor capacity. Growth is expected to outperform the market by 1-2%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the coke oven order a one-time project or recurring supply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said coke oven work is project-based but needs no capex; the 30,000+ tonne order covers 2 batteries, and at least 2 of 5 upcoming batteries are expected to follow, supporting the next 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Did inventory cost benefits show up in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the benefit from high-cost alumina inventory was used up, but higher-cost magnesia inventory (fused magnesia, DBM) offset it; double-digit price increases in some cases are expected to offset this and add margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 EBITDA outlook and how is the 2% outperformance measured?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 full-year EBITDA margin guided at about 13%, with Q1 expected to be strong. Outperformance is measured on volume, not price.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Dalmia FY26 revenue and margin, and what is the cement strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Dalmia revenue was INR 1,153 crores (+14%) with a 10.8% margin. Cement share fell to about 11% from 13%; the company is shifting to solution-based selling to large cement customers.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the fixed-cost benefit from iron making is in the margin, and where does margin settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify the iron-making fixed-cost absorption separately. On margin, it said 13% is achievable with mines, order book and 4PRO levers, and that without these it could have dropped to 10-11%.

qa_highlights.question: How big are the price increases and what drives Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases sought are 1-3% versus cost increases, effective from May. Q1 is also supported by pending price increases and the start of the cement season (May-September).

risks_watch: Goodwill impairment on Dalmia assets; management cites weaker exports, INR/USD volatility and new capacity.
Margin decline: Q4 EBITDA margin 12.1% against 13.7% in FY25, with 13% FY27 guidance needing price increases to stick.
Cement competition from Calderys, IFGL and smaller players; cement share down to about 11% of revenue.
Magnesia and energy cost inflation (China energy, freight), plus the West Asia conflict on input and freight costs; start-up costs on 3 new 4PRO contracts.
Recovery depends on the 30,000+ tonne coke oven order and on winning 2 of 5 upcoming coke oven batteries.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the FY27 outlook and the order book, but defensive on margins, which were repeatedly defended with price increases and the coke oven and mining levers. Evasive on quantifying iron-making fixed-cost absorption and on competitor details. Management also repeated its restructuring-complete position under analyst questioning.
key_quotes: Our performance reflects more than resilience. It demonstrates our ability to consistently create value while advancing our vision of driving progress in an ever-changing world.
We are projecting for next year 13% EBITDA.
We are sure we will be able to deliver a 13% or so.
So, if the market is growing by 6%-7%, we will be growing at 9%.
So, let's say that our cost increase is 0, then we are asking 1% - 3%.
